text:
Alice Nguyen: paging — NebulaHealth (enterprise VPC, dedicated pool) reporting per-tenant observability gap. customer sees missing traces and sparse spans for tenant `nebula-prod-42` since ~08:12 UTC, p95 latency for their requests spiking and our dashboards show metric partitions for their shard dropping to 0. they say logs are present in their app, but traces and metrics not linked in our observability. can oncall take? :rotating_light:

incident-bot: Incident created: #INC-20260315-NEBULA-OBSV. Paging Grace (oncall). Severity: P2. Notifying eng-runtime and eng-sre.

Grace (oncall): on it. linking logs/trace ids from customer would help. Alice, can you paste an example trace_id or a request id? also which dedicated pool?

Alice Nguyen: pool: dp-nyc-3c-nebula (dedicated). example request id: req_7f4a3c2b. customer says they see their app logs at ~08:12 but no spans from our side. they attached a short log snippet showing successful inference and a 200, but our trace UI shows no corresponding span.

Ben Perez: pinging eng-runtime — could be the tenant-forwarder partitioning index got mis-routed, or the per-tenant routing matrix lost the mapping for that tenant. I need the node list for the pool and the forwarder pod names. Emma, any recent deploys to forwarder control-plane?

Emma Seo: I didn't see a control-plane deploy in the last 12h. I do see spikes of 429s from the forwarder to the obsv-ingest endpoint at ~08:11:56. quick grep of forwarder logs for `nebula-prod-42` shows a repeated line: `WARN forwarder: tenant lookup miss for tenant=nebula-prod-42, fallback=none`. after that, we see repeated `HTTP 403` from auth-check when trying to push spans. full log excerpt:

```
Aug 15 08:11:56 forwarder-4 jvm[proc]: WARN forwarder: tenant lookup miss for tenant=nebula-prod-42, lookup_key=shard-17
Aug 15 08:11:57 forwarder-4 http: POST https://obsv-ingest.internal/v1/spans -> 403 Forbidden (auth: token expired)
Aug 15 08:11:58 forwarder-4 http: retry 1/3 -> 403
```

Grace (oncall): 403 from ingest + tenant lookup miss = likely forwarder had expired ephemeral key for that tenant mapping or the mapping sync job failed. can we confirm if the tenant-config-sync cron ran? Dan, can you check the config-sync job logs and the KMS rotation events?

Dan Roberts: looking. config-sync for dedicated pools runs every 5m; last successful sync for dp-nyc-3c-nebula was at 08:05. next scheduled was 08:10 but shows `error: unable to fetch mapping: rpc timeout`. KMS rotation events show a key refresh at 07:58, no issues. but the sync job did report increased latency to config-store at 08:09-08:11. suspect transient network egress issue to config-store partial reads -> mapping absent -> forwarder falls back and gets auth errors.

Frank (Solutions): FYI NebulaHealth customer impact: they report ~7% of requests got >3s extra latency and were retried client-side. no customer data loss reported, but they can't see traces which is blocking their internal SRE correlation. they want ETA on visibility restore for postmortem.

Ben Perez: proposed immediate mitigation steps: 1) re-route tenant `nebula-prod-42` to global-forwarder (bypass per-pool mapping) 2) force a config-sync for dp-nyc-3c-nebula and rotate ephemeral token for that tenant mapping 3) restart forwarder pods for the pool to pick up mapping. I'll prepare the k8s commands for 1 & 3.

Ben Perez: run to re-route (on control-plane cluster):

```
# apply temporary override to route tenant to global forwarder
kubectl -n control-plane patch cm tenant-routing --type=json -p '[{"op":"add","path":"/overrides/nebula-prod-42","value":"global-forwarder"}]'
# trigger rollout for the control-plane config to push override
kubectl -n control-plane rollout restart deployment/routing-pusher
```

Grace (oncall): Ben, while you do that I'll escalate network ops to check config-store egress in the pool's AZ. Emma, can you tail forwarder logs during the change and post any 403/lookup-miss lines? CarlaBot, start an ephemeral page to the customer success channel to give them an ETA (10-15m) and let them know we're doing a routing override.

CarlaBot: Notifying #customer-success: "NebulaHealth: We're investigating missing traces for your tenant nebula-prod-42 in dp-nyc-3c-nebula. We're applying a temporary routing override to restore visibility. ETA 10-15m. Please expect a follow-up."

Emma Seo: watching logs. after the config-patch and routing-pusher restart (08:17:20) I see the following sequence: two forwarder pods pick up override, subsequent POST to obsv-ingest now returns 200 for spans from tenant=nebula-prod-42. trace samples start appearing in the UI ~08:17:55. log excerpt:

```
Aug 15 08:17:21 forwarder-2 http: POST https://global-obsv-ingest.internal/v1/spans -> 200 OK
Aug 15 08:17:22 forwarder-2 cache: tenant override applied tenant=nebula-prod-42 -> global-forwarder
```

Grace (oncall): good. Frank (Solutions) — can you confirm with NebulaHealth whether they see traces back in their UI?

Frank (Solutions): customer confirmed at 08:19 they can see spans for the previously-missing requests and correlation is restored. they asked if we would do a follow-up to avoid recurrence.

Ben Perez: next steps to prevent recurrence: - fix config-store egress issue in dp-nyc-3c-nebula (NetOps) - add a fallback mapping in routing service to default to global-forwarder on lookup error (short-term) - add alert on `forwarder: tenant lookup miss` to page earlier - make config-sync retries more resilient and surface detailed error in control-plane dashboard. I'll open PRs for fallback and alerting.

Dan Roberts: NetOps confirmed transient egress latency to config-store for the pool's AZ between 08:08-08:12. they've queued a follow-up to stabilize the route and will provide a blameless RCA.

Grace (oncall): I'll keep the incident open for 1h for monitoring, then transition to postmortem. Please add any logs/commands/PR links to the incident ticket #INC-20260315-NEBULA-OBSV. Good job everyone. :thumbsup:

Alice Nguyen: thanks all. adding a note for the postmortem: customer impact = missing traces (visualization) + 7% elevated latency; no data loss, mitigation = routing override + forwarder restart, time to restore ~5m after applying override.

CarlaBot: Incident status updated: mitigated -> monitoring. Playbook: create postmortem draft and assign to Ben Perez (eng-runtime) and Dan Roberts (eng-sre).

Grace (oncall): closing handoff — I'll do the runbook writeup and link to the incident ticket. if anyone sees new regressions for this tenant or pool, re-ping here.

Ben Perez: PRs opened: fallback routing (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/432) and forwarder-alerting (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/119).

Dan Roberts: adding config-sync logs and NetOps traceroute output to #INC-20260315-NEBULA-OBSV.

Grace (oncall): last note — since this affected an enterprise VPC dedicated pool, schedule a brief sync with customer and solutions to review SLA impact and confirm postmortem. Closing thread in 30m if stable.
